provenance.instrument: Lancaster Township (Lancaster County) Code Chapter 280 Zoning (Ord. No. 2012-04, 8-20-2012, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2022-11-14 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-14: Ord. No. 2026-05 (2026-09-14) 'Zoning Amendment', Chapter 280, and Ord. No. 2024-01 (2024-04-08) 'Rezoning', PDF only, not read.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2022-11-14'. Ord. No. 2026-05 (zoning amendment) and Ord. No. 2024-01 (rezoning) are New Laws, not yet in the code text.
provenance.code_caution: The online code is current only to 2022-11-14. Two zoning New Laws are not yet in the code text (PDFs, not opened). Ord. No. 2026-05 (2026-09-14): its search excerpt permits non-vehicular campgrounds in the Industrial District by conditional use, with a new definition and a new Section 280-904. Ord. No. 2024-01 (2024-04-08) is a rezoning of the NCM site. A code search for 'accessory dwelling', which also covers New Laws text, found only the codified sections, so neither is read as touching the ADU rules.
checks: 'Accessory dwelling unit': 'An independent dwelling unit subordinate to and added to, created within, or detached from a principal single-family detached dwelling' (280-201). A permitted use in R-1 only (280-402A). R-2 and R-3 do not list it
At most 40% of the total square footage of the single-family detached house. One per lot. The lot meets all other single-family detached dimensional requirements of the district (280-1502A, B, C)

The owner lives in the house or in the accessory unit. Occupants of both units together may not exceed the family definition: any number of relatives, or not more than three unrelated people (280-1502D, E, 280-201)
Architecturally consistent with the house. Building permit before construction (280-1502F, G)

Parking: 'Accessory dwelling unit: one space per accessory dwelling unit, in addition to the parking required for the principal single-family detached dwelling use' (280-1303Q). The house needs two spaces per dwelling unit (280-1303B). Three in all

R-1 lot area is written 'per dwelling unit': 15,000 sq ft with public sewer and water, 32,000 with public sewer only, 43,560 otherwise (Table 4-1). The accessory unit is 'An independent dwelling unit' (280-201), and 280-1502C asks the lot to meet 'all other' single-family detached dimensional requirements. Whether the per dwelling unit lot area also applies to the accessory unit is not said. Ask the Zoning Officer
Accessory structures: not in the front yard and at least 15 ft from all front yards, 6 ft side and rear yards, 25 ft high (280-406)
'Lot coverage' is impervious cover (280-201): 35% in R-1 with public sewer and water

R-2 and R-3 permit two-family dwellings (with public sewer and water: 6,000 sq ft per unit in R-2, 5,000 in R-3). A building that existed before July 17, 1972 may be converted to a multifamily dwelling (three or more units, 280-201) by special exception in any residential district (280-502M, 280-602N, 280-1605)

Residential infill development is a conditional use in R-1, R-2 and R-3 on a tract of five acres or less that existed as a single tract when the section was adopted, with lot and yard standards set from the existing block (280-404C, 280-504C, 280-604C, 280-1530). An open space development may include 'Residential conversion units in accordance with the provisions of § 280-1605' (280-1523C(1)). Both are development plans, not a permit for one added unit

R-2 and R-3 yard tables give rows only for a single-family detached dwelling 'without public sewer' (side 12 ft, rear 35 ft) and 'with public water and public sewer' (Tables 5-2, 6-2). A lot with public sewer and no public water has no row of its own. The file uses the 'without public sewer' yards for it, which is an inference
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Lancaster Township (Lancaster County) Zoning Officer. Read on eCode360 (LA1280) in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. LA3847 on eCode360 is Lancaster Township, Butler County (Chapter 300), not this town. Code search (all content, New Laws included) for 'accessory apartment', 'accessory dwelling', 'in-law', ECHO, 'elder cottage', granny, relative, 'housekeeping unit', caretaker, 'guest house', 'accessory living' and 'tenant house' found 280-201 (ADU), 280-1502 and 280-402A. A search for 'accessory dwelling' alone found the same and 280-1303Q. Read in full: 280-1502, Articles IV (R-1) and V (R-2), 280-1605, and the definitions of accessory dwelling unit, family and lot coverage. Article VI (R-3) read in full. 280-1303 read in full. Not read: LC, GC, I and S use lists, height exceptions (280-1610), nonconforming lots (280-1703), the residential infill development definition (280-201), Ord. No. 2026-05 and 2024-01 (PDFs). Fix round 2026-11-14 after an independent review, read again in the code: parking verified (280-1303B, Q), the R-3 row completed (Tables 6-1, 6-2, 280-606), the R-2 public-sewer-only yards marked as an inference, residential infill development (280-1530) and open space conversion units (280-1523C) added, the multifamily definition read (three or more units).

term.note: 'An independent dwelling unit subordinate to and added to, created within, or detached from a principal single-family detached dwelling.'

status.note: A permitted use in R-1, subject to 280-1502. Building permit.

scope_districts.note: Only R-1 lists the accessory dwelling unit. R-2 and R-3 do not (280-502, 280-602).

status_outside.note: R-2 and R-3 permit two-family dwellings, not an accessory dwelling unit. LC, GC, I and S use lists were not read.

path.note: Permitted use. 'A building permit for an accessory dwelling unit must be approved and issued prior to its construction.'

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Two-family dwelling in R-2 or R-3
value.conditions: Two-family dwellings are a permitted use with public sewer and public water: 6,000 sq ft per dwelling unit in R-2 (12,000 for two), 5,000 in R-3 (10,000 for two). Lot coverage (impervious) 45% in R-2. Conventional development of 10 or fewer dwellings on 15 acres or less.
value.note: Converting an existing house into a two-family dwelling is read as this use. Not an ADU listing.

value.name: Conversion of a building that existed before July 17, 1972 into a multifamily dwelling
value.conditions: Zoning Hearing Board approval. No extension of the building except for access or safety. Lot area per existing and proposed dwelling unit: 8,000 sq ft in R-1, 4,000 in R-2, 3,000 in R-3.
value.note: A multifamily dwelling is 'A building containing three or more' dwelling units (280-201). Not a path for one added unit. An open space development in R-1 may also include such residential conversion units (280-1523C(1)(a)).

value.name: Residential infill development
value.conditions: Board of Supervisors conditional use. A tract of five acres or less that existed as a single tract when the section was adopted. Lot area, yards, height and design set from a study of the existing block, deviating from the district rules where they do not fit the neighborhood.

requires.condition: The tract is five acres or less and existed as a single tract when the section was adopted

value.note: A development of the tract with its own plan, not a permit for one added unit. The definition of residential infill development (280-201) was not read.

requires_conforming_lot.note: 'The lot shall comply with all other single-family detached dwelling dimensional requirements of the pertinent zoning district.'

districts_read_no_listing.note: Use lists read. No accessory dwelling unit.

types_allowed.note: 'Added to, created within, or detached from a principal single-family detached dwelling.'

max_share_of_house.note: 'Shall not exceed 40% of the total square footage of the principal single-family detached dwelling structure.'

max_height_ft.note: Accessory structures in R-1: 'Maximum height: 25 feet.'

front_yard_barred.note: 'With the exception of patios and decks, accessory structures shall not be permitted in the front yard', and at least 15 ft from all front yards.

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: Accessory structures have their own 6 ft side and rear yards.

owner_occupancy.note: 'The owner of the property must maintain principal residency in either the principal single-family detached dwelling structure or the accessory dwelling unit.'

family_only.note: No relationship rule. The total of occupants is capped.

occupancy.value: Occupants of the house and the accessory unit together may not exceed the family definition: any number of relatives, or not more than three unrelated people.
occupancy.note: How the combined cap treats a related household in one unit and an unrelated tenant in the other is not settled. Ask the Zoning Officer.

max_adus.note: 'There is a limit of one accessory dwelling unit per lot.'

spaces_required.note: 'Accessory dwelling unit: one space per accessory dwelling unit, in addition to the parking required for the principal single-family detached dwelling use.'

total_on_site.note: Two spaces for the house ('two spaces for each dwelling unit', 280-1303B) and one for the accessory dwelling unit.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling with public sewer and public water: '15,000 per dwelling unit'. Width 65 ft at the street, 100 ft at the setback line, depth 150 ft.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Written 'per dwelling unit'. The ADU is 'An independent dwelling unit' (280-201), and 280-1502C asks the lot to meet 'all other' single-family detached dimensional requirements. Whether the per dwelling unit lot area also applies to the ADU is not said. Ask the Zoning Officer.

setback_front_ft.note: Local road. 30 ft on a collector, 40 ft on a minor arterial, 50 ft on a principal arterial. Average of adjacent buildings within 100 ft where closer.

max_building_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage (impervious surfaces)': impervious cover, not buildings alone (280-201). No separate building coverage, so it is stored as the cap on buildings.

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: Accessory structures: not in the front yard, 15 ft from all front yards, 6 ft side and rear, 25 ft high (280-406).

value.when: No public sewer (public water only or none)

utility_rows.note: The ADU is an independent dwelling unit (280-201). Whether these per dwelling unit figures also apply to it is not said. Ask the Zoning Officer.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling with public sewer and public water: '10,000 per dwelling unit'. Width 50 ft at the street, 75 ft at the setback line, depth 125 ft. Two-family dwellings: 6,000 sq ft per dwelling unit.

setback_front_ft.note: Local road. 30 ft on a collector, 40 ft on a minor arterial, 50 ft on a principal arterial. Average of adjacent buildings within 100 ft where closer.

setback_side_ft.note: With public water and public sewer. 12 ft without public sewer.

setback_rear_ft.note: With public water and public sewer. 35 ft without public sewer.

max_building_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage (impervious surfaces)': impervious cover, not buildings alone (280-201). No separate building coverage, so it is stored as the cap on buildings.

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: Single-family detached lots. Not in the front yard, 15 ft from all front yards, rear 6 ft, 25 ft high (280-506).

value.note: Single-family detached: '32,000 per dwelling unit', width 65/100 ft, lot coverage (impervious) 25%. Table 5-2 has no yard row for public sewer without public water. The 12 ft side and 35 ft rear are the 'without public sewer' yards, used here as an inference.

utility_rows.note: Lot area and coverage from Table 5-1. The yards in the public sewer only row are an inference (Table 5-2 has no such row).

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling with public sewer and public water: '10,000 per dwelling unit'. Width 50 ft at the street, 75 ft at the setback line, depth 125 ft. Semidetached and two-family: 5,000 sq ft per dwelling unit.

setback_front_ft.note: Local road. 30 ft on a collector, 40 ft on a minor arterial, 50 ft on a principal arterial. Average of adjacent buildings within 100 ft where closer.
